title: Mining Tensor/Neuron-Level Sparsity to Maximize Mixture-of-Experts Potential in Post-Training and Inference
claim: Activation magnitude is highly uneven across both units and their sub-components, revealing large unexploited sparsity that can be exploited.
layout: Single heatmap with colorbar at right, a method diagram partly visible beside it
description: A large heatmap shows accumulated absolute activation values for neurons across the 64 experts of one MoE layer. The x-axis is neuron index, with ticks from about 350 to 1000. Rows are experts, so the y-axis carries the tensor-level view. The colormap runs from pale green (low) to deep blue (about 20k), and a vertical colorbar labeled 'Accumulated Activation' sits to the right. Most cells are very pale. A few horizontal bands are darker, which means some experts are much more active. Sparse dark vertical flecks within the bands mark individual high-activation neurons. The crop is cut off. At the bottom right, part of an orange rounded box with blue triangles and a yellow box (a method diagram) is visible, but only partially. The eye is drawn to the dark horizontal stripes.
caption: Visualization of accumulated absolute activation values for each neuron across 64 SwiGLU FFN experts in a single MoE layer OLMoE (Muennighoff et al., 2025) model during inference, highlighting tensor-level sparsity (y-axis) and neuron-level sparsity (x-axis) inherent to MoE architectures.
abstract: Mixture of Experts (MoE) has emerged as a mainstream architecture for Large Language Models (LLMs), balancing computational efficiency with model scalability. While prior work has explored increasing tensor-level sparsity via finer-grained expert configurations during pre-training, we identify significant unexploited sparsity at both the tensor and neuron levels during post-training and inference. To leverage this, we propose complete expert partition for post-training and threshold-based token-expert dropping for inference. These techniques improve the Mixtral-8$\times$7B model's average accuracy by 1\% across nine downstream benchmarks (notably 4\% on GSM8K). To further optimize the accuracy-efficiency trade-off for inference, we introduce dual-threshold token-expert dropping with partial expert partition and reconstruction. Our approach yields a 1.19$\times$ MoE speedup and a 0.5\% accuracy gain on Mixtral-8$\times$7B when combining post-training and inference optimizations. For inference-only optimization on OLMoE-Instruct and DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, we achieve up to 1.41$\times$ MoE speedup with a negligible accuracy loss ($<$0.5\%).
